title: K-Dwarf Dominance in Long-Lived Biospheres: Convergent Evidence from Stability and Metallicity Filters
key_finding: Two independent mechanisms converge on K-dwarf dominance: Phi-consciousness stability filter (Exp 4: 43.3% K) and TNG metallicity filter (Exp 5 refined: 60.6% K). Observer populations self-select to super-solar metallicity (mean 1.31 Z☉) even when galactic distribution peaks sub-solar (0.77 Z☉).
entropy_evolution_note: Life needs entropy for evolution — not low entropy globally, but steady energy flux in open thermodynamic systems enabling local order through entropy export. K dwarfs provide this optimally.
abstract: Long-term biological stability and sustained evolution require stars balancing longevity with environmental consistency. K dwarfs emerge as optimal hosts — longer-lived than G-type, far more stable than M dwarfs, with steady energy flux supporting open-system thermodynamics. The flare_denom critical transition at 2.5 maps directly to JWST-measurable M-dwarf atmospheric retention timescales.
